newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar slips vs yen in Tokyo on Japan rate fears.
newsitem.headline: Dollar slips vs yen in Tokyo on Japan rate fears.

text.p: *Dollar slipped against yen in afternoon Tokyo on market talk that Japanese wire service reported senior official of ruling LDP talking about possibility of interest rate rise.
*But greenback supported on short-covering interest near 116.10 yen for now.

*Dealers said impact from market talk about rate rise may be short-lived due to growing market perception that imminent rise in Japan's official discount rate is unlikely following weaker-than-expected industrial output data on Thursday.
*Dip below 116 yen possible if dollar clearly breaks below 116.10 yen, but next support point seen near 115.95 yen, a dealer at European bank said.
*Dollar's topside remains heavy on exporter offers near 117.60 yen and above and possible option-related sales.
*A trust bank dealer said stop-loss buying orders may emerge near and above 117 yen, but no strong buying incentives detected on upside in order to hit those stops.
0300 GMT - Dollar held on to small gains vs yen and mark by midday Tokyo, with falls in Japanese government bond yields and dips in Tokyo stocks supporting greenback.
*Dollar lacked energy to rise decisively above 116.50 yen due to hedge sales by investors, sell orders by Japanese exporters, and option-linked selling near 117 yen, dealers said.
*Yield of key 182nd 10-year cash Japanese government bond fell 10 basis points to 2.530 percent in late morning Tokyo. Nikkei stock average down 45.40 points or 0.22 percent at 20,266.83 at midday.
*Ruling Liberal Democratic Party's (LDP) administrative reform panel said on Friday it would recommend that the government raise interest rates in the future.
